text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Nigeria's ruling military council will soon meet to deliberate on recommendations that civil servants should get a salary increase.

- Ijaw and Itsekiri communities have levelled new allegations against each other over the violence which has erupted around the midwestern town of Warri, affecting oil production by Royal Dutch Shell's Nigeria unit.
- Central bank turns down request by banks for an extension of the deadline for the installation of machines that can separate naira notes fit for circulation from those which should be withdrawn.
- Traffic has been on the decline at Lagos and Tincan ports since the beginning of 1997 due to factors arising from ongoing reforms.
- Labour leaders said there would be no celebrations on May Day in Nigeria this year because of government decrees which have crippled the labour movement.
- Pilots' association calls for airlines to be allowed to operate only if they have a large enough capital base to ensure they can work for at least five years.
- Resident representative of the International Finance Corporation says the new Central Securities Clearing System running at the stock exchange could encourage foreign investment in Nigeria.
- Investors wishing to buy shares on the Nigerian Stock Exchange may in future have to pay up front instead of paying on delivery, a stock exchange official says.
